newsitem.title: UK: Britain's postal workers vote to resume strikes.
newsitem.headline: Britain's postal workers vote to resume strikes.

text.p: Britain's Royal Mail said on Wednesday that a postal workers' vote to resume strike action over a long-running dispute would drive away customers and threaten jobs.
Postal workers belonging to the Communication Workers' union voted 61 percent in favour of resuming the strikes over so-called new team-working proposals.
The union is talking to management over this issue and said it wanted the current round of talks to succeed.

Union general secretary Alan Johnson said in a statement the 78 percent turnout for the ballot showed the extent of members' support for the union leaders' position, giving them a strong mandate to reject Royal Mail's proposals.
"I would say we would use that mandate to persuade Royal Mail that they need to eliminate the three evils of our industry - high wastage, long hours and low morale."
The union has already staged eight strikes with the last one a 24 hour stoppage on September 2.

Royal Mail assistant managing director Ken Wright said, "The last thing Royal Mail and its customers needs are more strikes." He said in a statement that this would result in the government lifting the letter monopoly and leaving Royal Mail wide open to competition from its rivals.
Wright said that informal talks had begun last week on new proposals put forward by the union and there was now a real opportunity for both Royal Mail and the union to resolve the dispute.
The union said its executive would meet on Tuesday to review the situation further.
